analyst_view.overall: A top-five meeting: Girona (4th) and Eibar (5th) are level on 24 points, Eibar with a game in hand (Castellón away was postponed after Jesús de Miguel's death) but no league win in five, the latest 1-1 at home to Cádiz. Quique Álvarez's Girona came from behind to win 2-1 at Oviedo, have the second-best defence (13 conceded) and should have Vanat (five goals) and Holmes back from international duty; they miss Álex Moreno (fifth yellow), Bryan Gil, Jastin García and Furtado, all already in the numbers. Jokin Aranbarri's Eibar lost left-backs Juan Bernat (hamstring tear) and Imanol García de Albéniz (calf tear) and centre-back Unai Elgezabal (ankle) at the start of November, none on the brief's list; I found no update on their return. No referee is named and team news for this match was thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already adjust for Girona's absences. Eibar's defensive injuries (Bernat, García de Albéniz, Elgezabal) are not in the numbers, though they have already missed recent games, so part of it shows in Eibar's form; I add only a little, to about 2.25.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 5.8 of them Girona's as the side that usually controls the ball at Montilivi, and they already add some for Eibar conceding lots of corners lately. Nothing in the news changes that, so I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards, with Girona (35 yellows) more booked than Eibar (25). A top-five game has some edge, but no referee is named and nothing points to extra tension, so I stay at 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, 18 of them Girona's. Vanat and Holmes returning helps Girona, but they are part of the side the ratings know, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, already lifted by Eibar conceding many on target lately. Eibar's defensive absences are reflected in my small goals lean, and the effect on accuracy is small, so I stay at 9.1.
